title: Blues Jam @ Cadieux Café

event_venue_information:
Cadieux Café

Cadieux Café is a Belgian-style café and bar on Detroit's east side known for feather bowling — a rare Belgian lane sport played almost nowhere else in the country — alongside a deep list of Belgian beers and mussels.

Atmosphere and Setting

The café has the feel of a European tavern transplanted to Detroit's Morningside neighborhood, with a loyal local following and a calendar that mixes trivia nights, feather bowling leagues, and live music.

Blues Jam

Every Monday from 8:00 to 11:00 PM, Cadieux hosts a blues open jam led by Tosha Owens and The Stable Dudes, with a $5 suggested donation at the door.

Other Programming

Beyond the Monday jam, Cadieux Café regularly books local bands and runs its long-standing feather bowling leagues.

Good to Know

Cadieux Café is located at 4300 Cadieux Road on Detroit's east side near the Grosse Pointe border.

title: Open Mic @ Dessert Oasis Coffee Roasters (Detroit)
event_description: A welcoming weekly open mic for musicians and spoken word performers at a downtown Detroit coffee and dessert café. Bring your own instrument.
event_venue_information:
Dessert Oasis Coffee Roasters

Dessert Oasis Coffee Roasters, known locally as DOCR, is a downtown Detroit coffee shop and dessert café on Griswold Street with a loyal following for its pastries, coffee, and community programming.

Atmosphere and Setting

The café has a bright, welcoming coffeehouse feel, with tables cleared for performers on open mic nights and no stage separating musicians from the crowd.

Open Mic Night

Every Monday, DOCR hosts an open mic run by Samuel Sprague of Dirt Room. Sign-up starts at 6:30 PM and the mic runs from 7:00 to 9:00 PM, with 10 to 15 minutes per performer. Musicians and spoken word performers are welcome; performers should bring their own instruments, and stand-up comedy is not part of the format.

Other Programming

DOCR's Ferndale location runs a separate weekly open mic on Tuesdays, and both cafés otherwise operate as full-service coffee and dessert shops.

Good to Know

This DOCR location is at 1220 Griswold Street in downtown Detroit.

event_venue_information:
The Commons

The Commons is a combined laundromat and community café on Mack Avenue on Detroit's east side, built as a neighborhood gathering space with resources for the surrounding community alongside its coffee and sandwich counter.

Atmosphere and Setting

Upstairs, a large windowed room hosts community programming for The Vision Detroit, a nonprofit collective supporting Detroit artists. Chairs are arranged with a center aisle, and performance nights add live painting and creative activities alongside the open floor.

Open Mic

The Vision Detroit periodically hosts a free community open mic here welcoming artists of all kinds — singers, rappers, poets, and more — with sign-up through an online form that also accepts uploaded music files.

Other Programming

Beyond its open mic nights, The Commons functions as a working laundromat and café with posted resources for utility assistance, tutoring, and voter registration.

Good to Know

The Commons is located at 7900 Mack Avenue on Detroit's east side.

venue_name: Gate Keeper Bar and Game Store
backline: PA keyboard and percussion set with a cajon provided
event_venue_information:

The house provides a PA, a keyboard, and a percussion set with a cajon, and the night closes with a giant improv jam open to any willing musician, backed by a DJ set. title: The Ark's Open Stage @ The Ark
event_description: A beloved listening-room open stage at Ann Arbor's nationally known nonprofit folk venue. Names are drawn for eight-minute sets.
venue_address: 316 S Main St, Ann Arbor, MI 48104
event_venue_information:
The Ark

The Ark is a nationally renowned nonprofit folk and acoustic music listening room in downtown Ann Arbor, a stop for touring singer-songwriters for over five decades.

Atmosphere and Setting

The Ark is built for listening — a genuine concert hall atmosphere rather than a bar, with supportive audiences and a stage that has hosted some of folk music's biggest names.

The Ark's Open Stage

Several times a month at 8:00 PM (doors 7:30 PM), The Ark hosts its Open Stage series. Names are drawn at 7:55 and 8:30 PM, and each performer gets eight minutes or two songs. General admission is $3, with free entry for students and Ark members; tickets are available at the door only.

Other Programming

Beyond Open Stage, The Ark's main calendar features ticketed concerts from touring folk, roots, and singer-songwriter acts throughout the year.

Good to Know

The Ark is located at 316 South Main Street in downtown Ann Arbor.

event_venue_information:

Atmosphere and Setting

As a municipal senior center, the space offers an informal, welcoming daytime setting rather than a bar or club atmosphere.

Ann Arbor Bluegrass Jam

On the second and fourth Wednesday of the month, from 7:00 to 9:00 PM (setup at 6:30 PM), the center hosts a bluegrass jam that has met for more than seven years. Participants pay $5; listeners attend free. The ensemble plays roughly 20 standard bluegrass tunes per session on banjos, guitars, fiddles, mandolins, hammered dulcimers, dobros, electric bass, and percussion.

Other Programming

As a senior center, the broader calendar includes fitness classes, wellness programs, and community services for adults 55 and older.

Good to Know
